study type: Nested case-control study within a birth cohort
cohort: The study involved a California birth cohort comprising 736 pediatric papillary thyroid cancer cases diagnosed at 0-19 years (born 1982-2011) and 36,800 birth year-matched controls.
finding: The study found statistically significant associations between perinatal exposure to ambient PM2.5 and outdoor artificial light at night (O-ALAN) and an increased risk of pediatric papillary thyroid cancer.
